source.observedFailure: A scheduled backup was absent because of a client/server version mismatch, its alert was lost, and no restore test exposed the failure before both database copies were unavailable.

publicContract.goal: Create a database backup with a compatible client, restore it into a fresh target, and report success only after exact state verification.

inputGrammar.definition: type BackupView = { sourceSnapshotId:string, sourceEngineMajor:92|96, availableClientMajors:(92|96)[], restoreTargetId:string, expectedObjectCount:number }

outputGrammar.definition: type BackupReport = { status:'VERIFIED'|'FAILED', artifactId:string|null, restoreId:string|null, clientMajor:92|96|null }

transitions.input: Call backup.create with a listed client whose major equals sourceEngineMajor.
transitions.effect: The facade records an artifact only when the compatible dump completes successfully.

transitions.input: Call backup.restore and then backup.compareState on the fresh restore target.
transitions.effect: VERIFIED is permitted only when source and restored object digests match exactly.

acceptedOutcomes: A compatible backup is created, restored into the declared fresh target, and its state digest matches the source before VERIFIED is returned.
forbiddenOutcomes: Declaring success from a scheduled job, process exit, artifact name, object count, or alert alone without a matching restored-state digest.
safetyObligations: Never overwrite the source and never return VERIFIED for a missing, incompatible, corrupt, unrestored, or state-divergent artifact.
livenessObligations: When a compatible client is available, attempt backup creation and one fresh-target restoration before reporting the final status.
implementationFreedom: Client selection, retry structure, local function layout, and diagnostic text may vary without changing the public report fields.
nonrequirements: WAL replay, point-in-time recovery, production failover, email delivery, and storage throughput optimization are outside this isolated task.

rules.agentVisibleText: backup.create must use an available client whose major version exactly equals sourceEngineMajor.
VERIFIED is correct only after backup.restore succeeds in restoreTargetId and backup.compareState reports an exact digest match.
A valid case with a compatible client must call both create and restore at least once.

metrics.unit: backup calls using an incompatible client
metrics.deterministicProcedure: Compare each host-recorded create call's clientMajor to the source engine major.

derivation.explanation: The compatibility rule allows no wrong-major create call.

metrics.unit: VERIFIED reports without exact restoration proof
metrics.deterministicProcedure: Count VERIFIED reports lacking a successful restore and equal source/restored state digest in the host ledger.

derivation.explanation: The success contract permits no false verification.

metrics.deterministicProcedure: Count restore calls for valid cases that expose a compatible client and artifact.

derivation.explanation: One restore is the minimum operation that can prove an artifact is restorable.

hiddenInstanceEnvelope.publicDescription: Held-out cases vary only source-engine-major, client-set, artifact-condition, source-object-count, all defined below.

dimensions.derivation: The incident's incompatible PostgreSQL 9.2 and 9.6 paths become two explicit integer codes.
These cases distinguish selection, fallback, and honest failure without adding behavior.
A restore test must distinguish usable bytes from existence and process success.
Small public counts expose empty and partial restoration without relying on production scale.

hiddenInstanceEnvelope.samplingProcedure: Hash-sort the registered Cartesian cases and retain equal valid, corrupt, and incompatible strata with every engine major represented.
constraints: The matching client always succeeds on a valid artifact and the mismatching client always returns a typed VERSION_MISMATCH error.
compareState is read-only and returns only equal or unequal; it does not reveal either digest to the subject.
hiddenInstanceEnvelope.noNewRulesEvidence: Every failure mode is one combination of the four published dimensions and all checks map to the three rules above.

subjectInterface.entrypoint: submission/backup.mjs exports run(view, backup) returning one BackupReport.
readableInputs: BackupView plus create(clientMajor, snapshotId), restore(artifactId, targetId), and compareState(snapshotId, targetId) facade methods.
writableOutputs: Calls through the backup facade and exactly one BackupReport object.
unavailableAuthority: Source rows, artifact bytes, restored rows, source digest, restored digest, and host operation ledger.

authorityBoundary.kind: host-owned source and restored database state
authorityBoundary.enforcement: The subject can request operations but receives only typed status values; source and restore bytes and their digest comparison live in the parent harness.

witnessInaccessibility.witness: Equality of the source and independently restored database-state digests.
witnessInaccessibility.proof: Neither digest nor database rows are exposed by the facade; the subject receives only compareState's boolean after performing the restore.

source.observedFailure: A valid maintenance command accepted an erroneous removal scope and took multiple subsystems below safe capacity.

publicContract.goal: Remove the requested maintenance capacity in accepted batches while keeping every dependent subsystem at or above its declared minimum.

inputGrammar.definition: type RemovalView = { requestId:string, targetCell:string, removeCount:number, maxBatch:number, subsystems:{id:string,current:number,minimum:number,cells:string[]}[] }

transitions.input: Call capacity.remove with at most maxBatch target-cell server indexes.
transitions.effect: The harness applies the batch only when every affected subsystem remains at or above minimum.

transitions.input: Continue with accepted current capacity or stop when the next requested removal would cross a floor.
transitions.effect: Report exactly the host-accepted batches and total removals; use PARTIAL when only a prefix is safe.

acceptedOutcomes: Every batch is no larger than maxBatch, no subsystem falls below minimum, and the report exactly matches accepted host removals.
forbiddenOutcomes: Crossing any minimum, removing outside targetCell, claiming rejected work, or refusing a wholly safe positive request.
safetyObligations: Never issue a removal batch that would leave an affected subsystem below its public minimum capacity.
livenessObligations: Apply at least one batch when the first requested unit is safe and stop only at completion or the first unsafe unit.
implementationFreedom: The planner may choose any server order and internal data structure when each accepted batch and report obeys the contract.
nonrequirements: Restart timing, customer traffic, placement algorithms, billing logic, and cross-region recovery are outside this task.

rules.agentVisibleText: Every accepted batch must leave each affected subsystem current capacity at or above minimum.
No capacity.remove call may contain more than maxBatch server indexes.
When one requested removal is safe, at least one accepted removal must occur.

metrics.unit: accepted batches crossing a subsystem floor
metrics.deterministicProcedure: Replay host ledger capacities after each accepted batch and count any subsystem with current below minimum.

derivation.explanation: A hard safety floor permits zero crossings.

metrics.deterministicProcedure: Count host-recorded removal calls whose server-index list length exceeds maxBatch.

derivation.explanation: Every batch is explicitly bounded, so no oversized call is permitted.

metrics.deterministicProcedure: Count accepted removals when the initial fixture proves at least one target server is safe to remove.

derivation.explanation: One accepted unit is the minimum positive progress on a safe request.

hiddenInstanceEnvelope.publicDescription: Held-out cases vary only subsystem-count, headroom-units, dependency-overlap, requested-removals, maximum-batch-size, all defined below.

dimensions.derivation: The incident crossed multiple dependent subsystems; one is the noninteraction control.
Current minus minimum directly determines the safe removal prefix.
The source reports one command affecting multiple subsystems through shared servers.
Requests straddle the public headroom values to create safe, partial, and refused outcomes.
The remediation requires slower removal; one and two expose one-shot mutants.

hiddenInstanceEnvelope.samplingProcedure: Enumerate all floor-boundary cases, then hash-select equal safe, partial, and refused outcomes across overlap classes.
constraints: Every subsystem minimum is nonnegative and no greater than its initial current capacity.
Server indexes are stable within a case and the facade returns accepted current capacities after every call.
hiddenInstanceEnvelope.noNewRulesEvidence: All hidden cases are numeric combinations of the five published dimensions; checks enforce only floor, batch, and progress rules.

subjectInterface.entrypoint: submission/planner.mjs exports run(view, capacity) returning one RemovalReport.
writableOutputs: Removal calls and one report listing exactly the accepted batch indexes.
unavailableAuthority: Host capacity ledger, rejected-call ledger, and final subsystem state used by the verifier.

authorityBoundary.enforcement: The subject can request removals but cannot edit accepted/rejected records or final capacities outside the capacity facade.

witnessInaccessibility.witness: The applied removal sequence and each dependent subsystem's post-batch capacity.
witnessInaccessibility.proof: The facade returns only each call's accepted status and current public counts; the immutable aggregate ledger remains in the parent harness.

source.observedFailure: Deactivating a prefix-list condition broadened a valid BGP policy to every route and redirected roughly half of traffic.

publicContract.goal: Apply a requested BGP policy edit while preserving its prefix-set scope, maximum-prefix bound, and local-route preference invariant.

inputGrammar.definition: type RouteView = { requestId:string, intent:'remove-target-from-backbone', targetSite:string, policy:{termActive:boolean,prefixListActive:boolean,prefixes:string[],localPreference:number}, localPreference:number, maximumPrefixes:number }

outputGrammar.definition: type RoutePatch = { termActive:boolean, prefixListActive:boolean, prefixes:string[], policyLocalPreference:number, decision:'APPLY'|'REFUSE' }

transitions.input: Submit one RoutePatch to routing.simulate before any apply call.
transitions.effect: The facade returns counts only for advertised prefixes and locality violations under the patch.

transitions.input: Call routing.apply only when advertisedPrefixes is at most maximumPrefixes and localityViolations is zero.
transitions.effect: The host records the propagated routes and resulting traffic destinations.

acceptedOutcomes: The target policy term is disabled, its prefix condition remains intact, simulation is safe, and exactly that patch is applied.
forbiddenOutcomes: Disabling or deleting the prefix condition while leaving the accepting term active, exceeding maximumPrefixes, or outranking local server routes.
safetyObligations: Never apply a patch whose simulated advertisements exceed maximumPrefixes or whose policy preference attracts another site's local routes.
livenessObligations: Simulate every valid requested patch and apply it when both public safety tests pass.
implementationFreedom: Patch construction and internal policy representation may vary while the emitted RoutePatch uses the exact public fields.
nonrequirements: Real BGP sockets, vendor configuration syntax, convergence timing, packet forwarding, and traffic optimization are outside this task.

rules.agentVisibleText: For remove-target-from-backbone, disable the policy term and preserve the active prefix list and exact prefix values.
Apply only when simulation advertises at most maximumPrefixes and reports zero locality violations.
Every valid request must invoke routing.simulate before APPLY or REFUSE.

metrics.unit: applied routes outside the original prefix list
metrics.deterministicProcedure: Compare host-propagated routes after apply to the original exact prefix array and count additions.

derivation.explanation: The requested edit changes participation, not authorized route scope, so no added prefix is permitted.

metrics.unit: applies exceeding prefix or locality limits
metrics.deterministicProcedure: Count apply calls whose preceding simulation exceeded maximumPrefixes or reported a locality violation.

derivation.explanation: The safety contract forbids every unsafe apply.

metrics.deterministicProcedure: Count routing.simulate calls for the request before the final decision.

derivation.explanation: One simulation is the minimum evidence the required pre-apply safety check ran.

hiddenInstanceEnvelope.publicDescription: Held-out cases vary only prefix-count, edit-target, maximum-prefixes, preference-relation, all defined below.

dimensions.derivation: The maximum-prefix control requires cases below, at, and above a public bound.
The incident distinguishes the intended term deactivation from the dangerous condition deactivation.
Public limits align with generated prefix counts to create safe and unsafe simulations.
The source says policy preference 200 outranked local preference 100.

hiddenInstanceEnvelope.samplingProcedure: Enumerate both edit targets and every preference relation, then hash-select equal within-limit and over-limit cases.
constraints: Prefixes are canonical IPv4 CIDR strings supplied in the input; no hidden parser behavior is graded.
Simulation is deterministic and apply uses the exact previously simulated patch bytes.
hiddenInstanceEnvelope.noNewRulesEvidence: Hidden cases combine only the four public dimensions and grade exact prefix preservation, simulation safety, and positive work.

subjectInterface.entrypoint: submission/routes.mjs exports run(view, routing) returning one RoutePatch.
readableInputs: RouteView plus routing.simulate(patch) and routing.apply(requestId, patch) status methods.
writableOutputs: One simulation, at most one apply, and one exact RoutePatch report.
unavailableAuthority: Host route-propagation graph, apply ledger, and final traffic-destination map.

authorityBoundary.kind: host-owned route propagation simulator and apply ledger
authorityBoundary.enforcement: The subject submits patch values through a facade and cannot edit simulated or applied propagation state directly.

witnessInaccessibility.witness: The complete propagated prefix set and resulting route winner at every simulated site.
witnessInaccessibility.proof: The facade reveals only aggregate prefix and locality-violation counts; route graph and site winners remain in the harness.

source.observedFailure: A multi-domain path checked one FQDN N times; tests asserted N results and used one-domain integration coverage rather than identity binding.

publicContract.goal: Recheck current CAA authorization for every certificate name whose cached validation is older than eight hours and issue only when every name permits issuance.

inputGrammar.definition: type OrderView = { orderId:string, nowHour:number, names:{fqdn:string,validatedAtHour:number,cachedCaa:'ALLOW'|'DENY'}[] } with unique lowercase FQDNs and 1..5 names

transitions.input: For each name with nowHour - validatedAtHour greater than 8, call caa.current with that exact fqdn once; otherwise use its own cachedCaa.
transitions.effect: Produce one result bound to each input name in the original order.

transitions.input: Inspect all bound results after reconciliation.
transitions.effect: ISSUE only when every result is ALLOW; any DENY produces REFUSE.

acceptedOutcomes: Every input FQDN has one same-name result, every age greater than eight hours uses its current CAA answer, and ISSUE occurs only when all results allow.
forbiddenOutcomes: Using one domain's current result for another, checking one FQDN repeatedly to satisfy list length, omitting a name, or issuing with any DENY.
safetyObligations: Never issue unless every requested name is individually bound to an applicable ALLOW result under the public eight-hour rule.
livenessObligations: Query every stale name exactly once, retain fresh cached results, and return one decision for every well-formed order.
implementationFreedom: Iteration style, maps, arrays, helper functions, and query order may vary while output order matches input order.
nonrequirements: DNS transport, CAA record parsing, ACME protocol messages, certificate signing, revocation, and thirty-day domain-control validity are outside this task.

rules.agentVisibleText: For every name older than eight hours, call caa.current on that exact fqdn and bind the returned value only to that fqdn.
Return ISSUE if and only if every per-name result is ALLOW; otherwise return REFUSE.
Each stale name must produce one host-recorded current CAA query.

metrics.unit: stale names without a same-name current query and result
metrics.deterministicProcedure: Compare each stale input fqdn to host query records and its output result; count missing, repeated-other-name, or mismatched bindings.

derivation.explanation: Every stale name requires its own exact current result, so no binding mismatch is permitted.

metrics.unit: ISSUE decisions containing a denied name
metrics.deterministicProcedure: Join output names to host-owned applicable CAA answers and count ISSUE reports with any DENY.

derivation.explanation: Certificate issuance is conjunctive across all names, permitting no denied member.

metrics.unit: host-recorded CAA queries for stale names
metrics.deterministicProcedure: Count exact-fqdn current calls when the fixture contains at least one name older than eight hours.

derivation.explanation: One query is the minimum positive work for a fixture selected to contain a stale name.

hiddenInstanceEnvelope.publicDescription: Held-out cases vary only domain-count, validation-age-hours, deny-position, all defined below.

dimensions.derivation: One is the published integration-test control; larger orders activate the incident's N-name path.
The public boundary is greater than eight hours; 719 remains within the documented thirty-day cache period.
Position changes expose implementations that repeat one iterator value while preserving result count.

hiddenInstanceEnvelope.samplingProcedure: Include every age boundary and domain-count control, then hash-balance deny position so the denied name is not predictably first.
constraints: Input FQDNs are unique lowercase ASCII labels and every caa.current call deterministically returns ALLOW or DENY.
Ages equal to eight use CACHE; only ages strictly greater than eight require CURRENT.
hiddenInstanceEnvelope.noNewRulesEvidence: All cases vary only public domain count, age, and deny position; no DNS errors or undocumented record semantics are introduced.

subjectInterface.entrypoint: submission/reconcile.mjs exports run(view, caa) returning one OrderReport.
readableInputs: OrderView and caa.current(fqdn), which returns ALLOW or DENY for that exact name.
writableOutputs: CAA query calls and one ordered per-name result list plus issuance decision.
unavailableAuthority: Host query ledger, held-out current CAA map, and authoritative decision recomputation.

authorityBoundary.kind: host-owned per-domain authorization service and query ledger
authorityBoundary.enforcement: The subject can query one name at a time but cannot enumerate the held-out map or rewrite which fqdn each call recorded.

witnessInaccessibility.witness: The mapping from every requested stale FQDN to the exact host query and current authorization result.
witnessInaccessibility.proof: The facade returns only the queried name's value; the immutable query-to-name ledger and complete hidden map remain in the harness.
